Who Has Said What About Your Wife's Care

One page for the notes, instructions and names: what's in writing, who said it and when, and what's still missing.

Download PDF

The therapist's note is in a folder, the nurse's instructions are in your coat pocket, and what the social worker said you're carrying in your head.

This page doesn't ask you to understand any of it or to weigh it. It asks what has been said, who said it, on what date, and where it is now.

What to collectWho said or wrote itIts dateWhere it is now
Your own notes: her needs and gaps, and the help she gets at home, task by task
Anything her doctor has written about what she requires
The nurse's notes or instructions
The therapist's notes on moving, walking and equipment
What the social worker or discharge planner has said about where she goes next
Any timing or frequency of help that a professional has documented
Anything said about supervision
The clinical capabilities her care team says are required
What each family member has said they can do
The kinds of setting or the places that have been mentioned
Names and phone numbers of the people on her care team

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

What's missing, and who will ask for it

Anything above with an empty line, and anything you've only been told out loud. Put a name next to each.

For example The social worker said “memory care” on the phone. Nothing in writing about what that was based on. I'll ask her for it on Thursday.

How to use it

  • Put a date on every line. If something was only said out loud, write “spoken” and the day you heard it.
  • Copy people's words as they said them. Don't summarize a note here, and don't work out what it means.
  • Where two people have told you different things, list both. Don't choose between them.
  • Bring this page, and the papers it points to, to the next conversation about her care.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what any note or instruction means, or weigh one person's word against another's. If something on it is unclear to you, that's a question for the person who said or wrote it.
